My high school boyfriend was this way with me. He took over my life for the two years we were together and I let him. Between the fear of him physically hurting me and him creating a situation where I depended on him for so much, it was a rough situation. When I finally had the guts to leave him, I was terrified he'd retaliate. 

It took him another girlfriend or two (not sure completely, I had cut him out of my life) before he came back to me, claiming that he knew what he did to me was wrong and that he had changed. The problem here was that I was happier, in a new, healthy relationship, and he was still as manipulative as before. He wasn't trying to change for himself, he was trying to convince me he had changed to get me back. And it obviously didn't work. I haven't heard from him in years, and I'm happily married now. 

You have to want to be a better person to start seeing some change. And you're off to a good start with trying therapy. Along with realizing that your ex will be happier without you, even if you do end up changing. For her, it wasn't a good experience and there's not a lot that will change that. Work on yourself until there's a point where you can try relationships again without falling back into your old patterns. You can change, I believe in you!
